surfaces.name: Forever Twins
surfaces.oneLiner: Give an existing collectible a permanent, self-contained on-chain counterpart.
surfaces.coreLine: Your NFT can survive while the art disappears.

angles.premise: The token survives, the art it points at does not. A Forever Twin makes the collectible self-contained without breaking its collection identity or its holder relationship.
Most NFTs are a pointer to a server somebody is still paying for. Describe what happens when that stops, then describe the fix.
Bitcoin Pepes are the first public Forever Twins collection, powered by Xtrata and built with Fak.fun. Holders are claiming twins now.

surfaces.name: Suno More
surfaces.oneLiner: Inscribe the master, preserve attribution, and connect editions and remixes.

angles.premise: AI music is generated on a platform and lives at that platform's pleasure. Inscribing the master makes the recording outlast the account that made it.
Editions and remixes can point at the master on-chain, so credit survives without a rights database in the middle.

The player can be embedded elsewhere, so any site can carry a station it does not host.

surfaces.name: X Chess
surfaces.oneLiner: Chess on Stacks, where the board itself is a permanent inscription.
surfaces.coreLine: The board is not hosted. It is inscribed.

angles.premise: It is not a demo. Games are open and moves are being submitted, and every move is a signed transaction rather than a row in a database.
You do not join X Chess. You open a board, name your opponent or leave the seat empty, and share the link. There is no lobby, no queue, no matchmaking.
The anyone-else setting opens the board to the world and closes it to you, so the opener cannot quietly play both colours. Impossible rather than unlikely.
Tick sponsored and the contract sends your opponent their gas in the same transaction that opens the board. They can play with an empty wallet. No faucet, no airdrop, no signup.
Boil chess.com down until only the chess is left. Delete the servers, the accounts, the referee, the company. It still works.
The board is not hosted, it is inscribed. The artefact is the application. No app store, no download, no update.
The contract stores no position, no turn, no winner. Just a list of four character strings and the arithmetic to read them.
Ratings are stored nowhere. Anyone can recompute every rating from the chain and get the same number.

surfaces.notes: Went live 2026-08-11. Inscription 2988 is permanent and hardcodes the xchess-core-v1-canary contract, so it cannot be repointed at a differently named contract later. A large hand-written posting board of proven copy is at X-Chess/shots/tweets.html, with screenshots in X-Chess/shots/. Use it rather than inventing new lines, with two caveats: two of its posts are marked UNVERIFIED and still are, and five of them say a thing is 'on Bitcoin'. X Chess runs on Stacks, which is anchored to Bitcoin and mined by it through Proof of Transfer. Take the structure from those posts and fix the chain word. The linter rejects 'on Bitcoin'.
